topic: PPF 7.1% vs inflation 4.82%: real return explained
hook_pattern: contrarian number (7.1% isn't what you grow)
caption:
PPF pays 7.1% for October–December 2026, tax-free. Retail inflation was 4.82% in August. The difference, roughly 2.3 percentage points, is your real return: how much more your money can actually buy after a year.

That's the number worth comparing. A rate on its own tells you how many more rupees you'll have. Rate minus inflation tells you whether those rupees buy more than they did. When it is positive, your buying power grows. When it is negative, savings shrink quietly even as the balance goes up.

Two caveats: inflation changes every month, so the gap moves too. And for taxable savings, compare after tax, which narrows it further.

Save this for the next time you compare a rate. Send it to someone who thinks a fixed return is risk-free. Follow for one money fix a day.

Sources: small savings rate announcement (30 Sep 2026); retail inflation data for August 2026 as reported. Real return is a simple approximation.
For education only. Not investment advice.
